name: Luna 21 / Lunokhod 2
first: Second Soviet lunar rover; longest off-world drive (~39 km) for over 40 years
description: Luna 21 delivered Lunokhod 2, the Soviet Union's second crewed-controlled lunar rover, to Le Monnier crater on the southern edge of Mare Serenitatis in January 1973. The rover was driven from a control room in Crimea by a five-person team and traversed approximately 39 km over four lunar days — a record off-world distance that held until NASA's Opportunity rover passed it on Mars in 2014. Lunokhod 2 returned 80,000 television frames and 86 panoramas before dust contamination of its solar arrays ended operations.

events.label: TLI
events.note: Trans-lunar injection on the Blok-D upper stage.

events.label: LANDING
events.note: Soft landing in Le Monnier crater 1973-01-15. Lunokhod 2 rolled off ramps a few hours later.

events.label: ROVER ACTIVE
events.note: Five-person ground crew in Crimea began driving operations. Total traverse: ~39 km.
